text:
Your flight lands at Kansai Airport at 21:30 and you're staying in Kyoto. By the time you clear immigration, the last Haruka (22:16) may be gone. The bus keeps running until 23:20 👇

🕙 Late-landing plan in 3 steps (save it before you fly) 👉 https://japanbystation.com/kansai-airport-to-kyoto

✅ 1. CHECK THE CLOCK, NOT JUST THE PRICE

The Haruka is faster, about 75–80 minutes, but its last train leaves the airport at 22:16 on weekdays. The limousine bus to Kyoto Station keeps going: last departure from Terminal 1 at 23:20, arriving around 0:45.

✅ 2. KNOW HOW THE BUS WORKS

¥2,800, cash or ICOCA on board, suitcases in the hold. There are no reservations from the airport to Kyoto: first come, first seated, roughly every 20 minutes.

✅ 3. SLEEP NEAR THE HACHIJO EXIT

The bus stops in front of the Avanti building, opposite Kyoto Station's south exit. A hotel on that side means a short walk to bed instead of a taxi queue at 1 a.m.

🎫 FLYING IN EARLIER?

Then the Haruka wins. The visitor one-way ticket went up on 1 November 2026, from ¥2,200 to ¥2,700, and tickets bought before that stay valid.
